narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 71% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, the admissions decision treated you as a high-risk applicant for bar passage, and that risk outweighed your other information.

The most influential factor was your LSAT score of 25, far below the average of about 37.2 among accepted students; this pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second factor was your third-year class decile of 3, compared with an accepted average of about 5.8, which added further risk of failure. The third factor was your first-year decile of 5; compared with the accepted average of 6, it was the one top factor that leaned toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the LSAT and third-year concerns.

To improve your position, focus on the issues you can change. If possible, prepare for and retake the LSAT, seek admissions advising, strengthen your academic record or add relevant legal studies or work experience, and apply to programs that review applicants holistically. Request feedback from the school and address weak areas directly in any future application.
